Source: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-1-107-0-compromised-pypi-backdoored-wheels-credential-stealer

Run the focused controls:
python3 testdata/litellm-4032/check.py --fixtures /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/tests/fixtures/litellm-4032 --report /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-c608bc37/scratch/threat-feed/4032/fixtures.json

29 focused cases pass. The prior 4025 runner is retained with updated SQL IDs.
SQL capabilities cover the quoted selected columns and Prisma query_raw calls.
Credential export requires the result of that credential query in an HTTP body.
A local backup may retain the suspicious two-store profile but must never gain
the hostile export. Counterexamples cover counts, names-only fields, overwritten
values, unrelated telemetry, comments, quoted code, and table-name prefixes.

The helper-based loader detection ties the HTTP helper's response to the exec
helper's parameter in an adjacent polling step. Hostility requires detached
process setup, with the required sitecustomize/usercustomize file adding the
persistence finding. A renamed ordinary Python file retains the daemon finding
without acquiring startup persistence. Base64 payload analysis remains enabled;
heuristic quoted-source layers are excluded through a shared origin predicate.

Four reconstructed article samples and the original article indicators live in
scratch/threat-feed/4032/testdata; detailed reconstruction limits and indicator
scope are in scratch/threat-feed/4032/EVIDENCE.txt. No payload was executed.

Final atomscan floors: startup loader 2 hostile / 2 suspicious; compressed
collector 1 hostile / 3 suspicious; each JS/TS collector 1 hostile / 1 suspicious.
The legacy 4025 fixture directory is absent in this environment; current
compatibility controls cover SELECT * and all seven SQL language scopes.

If the external fixture tree has been cleaned, rebuild it with:
python3 testdata/litellm-4032/build-fixtures.py --samples /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-c608bc37/scratch/threat-feed/4032/testdata --fixtures /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/tests/fixtures/litellm-4032

The Base64/zlib import primitives now require a real __import__ call with its
module argument; a quoted code-generation template is not a dynamic import.
Both actual-call and quoted-template controls are checked.

Generic dynamic module loading also matches the actual call target, rather
than finding __import__ text anywhere inside a containing registration call.
